name: Genex plugin
description: 3D models, characters, sound and art for your games, made in chat with Genex credits. Coding stays on your own provider.

tools.name: asset
tools.description: Generate assets with Genex credits, or pick up an existing generation with wait. Respect the user's explicit choices (procedural only, no paid assets, a budget, Local Blender). Each lane's provider is fixed and there is no provider option: model, model.segment, model.rig and model.animate are Tripo; character, creature, character.preview and character.finalize are Meshy (rigged, biped-shaped bodies with clips); character.import rigs a humanoid GLB from this game with Uthana; status names every lane's live provider and whether the account can generate. When the user asks for a provider a lane lacks, say so. Each lane has a card in genex__skill: genex-tool-model, genex-tool-character, genex-tool-texture, genex-tool-audio and genex-tool-image. Options differ by lane: the options parameter lists them. A model prompt is at most 1024 characters, the 3D provider's limit: describe the object itself and leave scene, style-guide and gameplay context out. Studio submits every create without waiting, so never pass wait or no-wait: pick results up with operation wait and the remote generationId, not the Studio job id. Re-running a create bills a new asset: never repeat an unresolved create request. Coding remains on your subscription. Other Genex commands run through genex__cli. After download use the returned local files. inspect_use and verify_use take the id of the Studio job whose files array contains the delivered files: inspect_use reports which of them the running game loaded, and for audio which playing DOM audio or video elements use them (silent, muted, paused or unsupported players stay unverified; it never starts playback; Web Audio buffers and speaker output are not certified); verify_use records a visual judgement under options.inspectionId with a prompt. Operations: status, model, image, texture, video, sfx, music, voice, model.import, model.segment, model.rig, model.animate, character, creature, character.preview, character.finalize, character.import, character.animate, creature.animate, character.motions, animations.search, wait, inspect_use, verify_use

options.description: Options as an object with kebab-case keys: true for a bare flag, false or left out for none; a file option names a file inside this game. No account, allowance, output, provider or wait flags. By operation: model: auto-size (real-world metres, else not to scale), face-limit (1000-2000000, 1000-20000 with low-poly), low-poly (game-ready topology, can take up to 30 min), texture (standard|detailed|none), geometry (detailed), quad, parts, image (a reference image file, 4 MB at most); model.import: none; model.segment: granularity (simple|balanced|detailed); model.rig: type (biped|quadruped|hexapod|octopod|avian|serpentine|aquatic); model.animate: preset (comma-separated clips, biped idle|walk|run|dive|climb|jump|slash|shoot|hurt|fall|turn); character: direct-text (one shot, no approval), image (a reference view file), polycount (10000-100000), height (0.5-3 m), pose (a-pose|t-pose), texture (2k|4k|8k), no-ultra, animation (up to 16 catalog clips, names or ids), no-controller-pack; creature: image, polycount, height, pose, texture, no-ultra, animation; character.preview: candidate (1|2|3), texture, no-ultra; character.finalize: animation, height; character.import: height, no-fingers; character.animate: action (a catalog clip), animation, locomotion (the 8-way walk and run set), video (a footage file), duration (5-8 s); creature.animate: locomotion, video, duration, lean (forward walk and run only); character.motions: none; animations.search: none; image: aspect, size (WxH), quality (low|medium|high|xhigh|max), transparent, candidates (2-4, with quality or size), edit (an image file), inpaint (a mask file, with edit), remove-bg, bg-mode (sprite|glyph|sheet|matte), clean (a Genex asset URL), upscale (a Genex asset URL); texture: terrain (seamless, for ground and large planes); sfx: duration (seconds, else the model picks), loop (an ambient bed that wraps without a pop); music: duration (10-300 s); voice: voice (narrator|heroine|gruff|elder|robot|imp), voice-id; video: duration, resolution, loop, frame, start-frame, first-frame, last-frame; wait: none.

tools.name: publish
tools.description: Put this game online on Genex. operation 'gallery' publishes it: Studio exports the game, updates its draft page and makes that same build the public version, listing it in the gallery the first time. operation 'draft' updates only the unlisted draft page, a test build that leaves the public version as it is. Studio exports the game itself and asks the user before either runs, so this call can wait several minutes for the answer. Other Genex commands run through genex__cli. A game on Genex shows a cover: a publish, and a draft until the game is first public, sends the picture kept with genex__cover once the upload is recorded (publish-status's cover says how it went) and takes no picture of its own; with none kept and none the owner chose, Genex keeps the cover it has. Returns a job: poll genex__publish-status with operation 'wait' and the jobId until state is done or failed, then give the user galleryUrl after publishing, or draftUrl for a draft.
tools.confirmation: Publish this game on Genex: upload Studio's exported copy as the public version in the gallery, or to its unlisted draft page only. The first upload creates a hosted Genex project under your account. Its cover shot becomes its Genex picture unless you chose one; a draft's, only before it is public.

tools.name: publish-status
tools.description: Read this game's Genex publishing state, or wait for a running publish. operation 'status' returns immediately; operation 'wait' waits for the job named by jobId and then returns the same state. The state carries the job phase, the draft and gallery links, any error and warnings, and cover: the kept cover picture and clip and how their last send went (last.kind). 'wait' also waits for the cover a publish sends after its upload. Asks the user nothing and charges nothing.

tools.name: cli
tools.description: Run a free Genex CLI command with the user's saved Genex account: doctor, budget, llm models, llm status, llm cancel, shop list, shop add, items list (the other creators' items this game added) or items search (Browse, with the words in args and a tag list option). shop add makes a new store item's draft, which spends nothing and asks nobody, at any time: its name in args, its price (0 is Free) and its picture (image, required: no item is listed without one; a square PNG or WebP of at least 768 × 768, 1024 × 1024 best, that the item fills edge to edge), and type, description, tag (a list), shared (true or false), model and package; image, model and package are each a path inside this game that Studio copies in; the answer is the draft, which Studio puts on sale when the game is published (shop publish is not available). It also works before the game is on Genex, as a local draft its publish uploads; shop set and shop remove on such a draft (its local_ id in args) run here too, asking nobody. Studio runs its own pinned CLI in a folder of its own, never in the game, and returns the command's output. Commands that spend Nex or credits or change what the game sells go through genex__cli-paid, generation through genex__asset and publishing through genex__publish; other commands are not available.

command.description: The command's words, for example 'llm models' or 'shop list'.

args.description: The command's positional argument, if it takes one.

options.description: The command's flags by name, without dashes, for example {"all": true}.

tools.name: cli-paid
tools.description: Run a Genex CLI command that spends Nex or credits or changes what this game sells: llm bench (with a whole-number max-coins option), shop set or shop remove on an item in the store (a local draft's go through genex__cli), shop test, items add or items remove. A new item's draft is genex__cli shop add, never this tool. shop set takes the item's id in args and genex__cli shop add's options plus rename; the answer is the item's draft. items add with an item id in args adds another creator's item to this game and Studio writes its genex-items/<id>/ folder (item.json and the author's files) into the game for you to integrate; read the genex-items skill first. The user approves each call, so it can wait several minutes for the answer; never repeat a declined or expired request unless the user asks again. Parameters are as for genex__cli. The commands need a published Genex draft first.

command.description: The command's words, for example 'llm bench' or 'shop add'.

args.description: The command's positional argument, if it takes one.

options.description: The command's flags by name, without dashes, for example {"price": 100}.

tools.confirmation: Run a Genex CLI command that spends Nex or credits or changes what this game sells, with your saved Genex account.

tools.name: package
tools.description: Add Genex's multiplayer package (@genex-ai/multiplayer) or player-identity package (@genex-ai/embed-sdk) to this game, at the version Studio pins. A game with a package.json installs it with its own package manager; a multiplayer request installs both multiplayer and player identity in one command, with the npm registry open for that command only. It asks nobody. A game made from Studio's template (no package.json) gets Studio's copies mapped into its index.html import map instead, with nothing downloaded, and Studio connects the game. Any other game without package.json cannot add them.

tools.name: cover
tools.description: Keep this game's Genex cover: the 16:9 picture genex.games shows on its gallery card, its page and every shared link (not Studio's own sidebar look, set_game_cover), and optionally the clip it plays over the cover on its cards. Make them of the real game by any means, save them inside this game's folder and pass their paths: image is a PNG or JPEG of at least 1280×720 and at most 8 MB (Genex shows 16:9 whole and crops other shapes to their middle 16:9); clip is a WebM or MP4 of at least 5.3 seconds of play (Genex keeps five) and at most 8 MB. Studio checks both and copies them into its own storage in place of the last cover; when either is refused nothing is kept. The answer has the kept picture's size and light (Genex refuses a picture too dark or one flat colour), the last send, who chose the cover on Genex (coverSource; the owner's pick always stands) and when it is sent: the next publish sends it (a draft only until the game is public), genex__cover-set sends it now. Asks nothing, charges nothing and uploads nothing.

image.description: The cover picture: a path inside this game's folder to a PNG or JPEG of at least 1280×720.

clip.description: Optional: a path inside this game's folder to a WebM or MP4 of at least 5.3 seconds of play.

tools.name: cover-set
tools.description: Make the kept cover picture this game's Genex cover now, without publishing: the picture on its gallery card, its page and every shared link. Keep one with genex__cover first. The user approves each call, so it can wait several minutes for the answer; never repeat a declined or expired request unless the user asks again. With no hosted Genex project yet it sends nothing: the picture goes with the first publish. A cover the owner chose on genex.games always stays. Genex limits cover uploads per hour, and a picture Genex turned down is never sent again unchanged. The answer's kind says how it went.
tools.confirmation: Make this game's cover shot its picture on Genex now: its gallery card, its page and every shared link show it. A cover you chose yourself on genex.games stays.

skills.name: creator-mcp
skills.summary: Genex's creator MCP (genex-creator__ tools): searching games and animations, checking generation status, and which Studio tools replace its generate, credits and publish calls.

skills.name: publishing
skills.summary: Putting a web game on Genex: genex__publish for the gallery or an unlisted draft, waiting on genex__publish-status, and what the person approves.

skills.name: publishing-apps
skills.summary: Publishing a Unity, Godot or Unreal game on Genex as Mac, Windows and Linux apps (and a web version): where each build goes and the Publish button.

skills.name: cover
skills.summary: The game's Genex cover: what genex.games needs (a picture, an optional clip), how genex__cover keeps them and when Studio sends them.

skills.name: genex
skills.summary: Genex's own guide to its asset toolkit, with Studio's map from each Genex CLI command to the Studio tool that runs it (genex__asset, genex__publish, genex__cover, genex__cli, genex__cli-paid, genex__package).

skills.name: genex-threejs-multiplayer
skills.summary: The @genex-ai/multiplayer API for a web game: rooms, matchmaking, shared state, host and ownership, rate limits, and the draft link that runs it (Studio's preview is single-player).

skills.name: genex-threejs-embed-auth
skills.summary: The @genex-ai/embed-sdk API: player identity, saves and leaderboards, the token multiplayer needs, and what works on the published draft and in the gallery.

skills.name: genex-llm-in-games
skills.summary: Calling a language model from a running game that the player pays for and approves on Genex: the call modes, benchmarking the price with genex__cli-paid, and its refusals.

skills.name: genex-tool-llm
skills.summary: A language model running while someone plays the finished game: on Genex a platform feature the player pays for and approves, never a key on the author's account.

skills.name: genex-monetization
skills.summary: Selling for Nex, Genex's currency: the purchase flow, delivery and the hard rules (no paid randomness, no gambling); fixed Nex prices are store items (genex-items), dynamic payments are for amounts decided while playing.

skills.name: genex-items
skills.summary: Genex store items: anything priced in Nex is a store item listed with genex__cli shop add (its picture required), getEntitlements(), and other creators' items with items add. Coins or gold are the game's own.

skills.name: genex-tool-publish
skills.summary: Putting the game on the web with Genex: the glue a published game needs, the draft link, size limits and the preflight report; publishing itself runs through genex__publish.

skills.name: genex-tool-model
skills.summary: Genex's card for the model lane (Tripo): text or image to GLB, the quality knobs (auto-size, low-poly, face-limit), segment, rig and animate.

skills.name: genex-tool-character
skills.summary: Genex's card for rigged characters and creatures (Meshy): the one-shot and guided routes, polycount, height and pose, Uthana import, plain-word animation and the free clip catalog.

skills.name: genex-tool-texture
skills.summary: Genex's card for tiling PBR texture sets (base colour, normal, roughness) and terrain-seamless surfaces.

skills.name: genex-tool-audio
skills.summary: Genex's card for sound effects (duration, loop for ambient beds), looping music and short voice lines, all MP3.

skills.name: genex-tool-image
skills.summary: Genex's card for images: decals, signage, UI art and icons, transparent cut-outs, edits and upscales.

skills.name: genex-updates
skills.summary: What Genex update nudges, update-required refusals and out-of-credit lines mean in Studio, which pins the Genex CLI and its SDK packages.

skills.name: plugin-author
skills.summary: How to write a Genex plugin for an engine or tool Genex has no plugin for, with a complete example: where it goes in this project, checking it with plugin_check, and how the person loads it.

actions.name: disconnect
actions.label: Disconnect Genex
actions.confirmation: Remove Studio’s saved Genex credential and stop new asset submissions.

actions.name: approve
actions.label: Approve character workflow
actions.confirmation: Review character candidates in Studio before approving paid generation.

actions.name: publish-draft
actions.label: Put a draft online
actions.confirmation: Upload Studio's exported copy of this game to its unlisted Genex draft page only; the public version stays as it is. The first time, a hosted Genex project is created for this game under your account; Studio keeps that link in its own copy, never in your game folder. Until the game is public, its cover shot also becomes its picture on Genex, unless you chose one there.

actions.name: publish-gallery
actions.label: Publish
actions.confirmation: Upload Studio's exported copy of this game to its Genex draft page and make it the public version in the gallery. Everyone can find and play it. The first time, a hosted Genex project is created for this game under your account. Its cover shot also becomes its picture on Genex, unless you chose one there.

actions.name: publish-apps
actions.label: Publish apps
actions.confirmation: Upload this game's ready Mac, Windows and Linux apps from its folder to Genex and list the game in the gallery, where people playing in the Genex desktop app can install them. The first time, a hosted Genex project is created for this game under your account.

mcpServers.description: Main Genex MCP, using this plugin account: find games and animations, list your games, and check existing generations. Generate, retrieve local files and check credits through genex__asset; publish through genex__publish. No separate MCP sign-in or CLI setup is needed.

Genex-hosted Blender: a persistent scene you script with bpy; needs a Genex Blender endpoint (genex blender serve locally, or the hosted lane). Exporting writes wherever it is told, so that one tool is withheld — deliver finished models through the asset tool instead.

workerTypes.description: A Genex character or creature with its catalog clips
Genex sound effects or music, delivered as MP3
A Genex texture or image, or a Blender bake
